edition_note: Recovery edition. Overnight narrative stops at 09:29 ET; tape quotes are separate 10:14–10:24 ET snapshots, not live-refreshing. Cash indexes and Bitcoin are Nov 10 closes. Treasury quotes are Nov 10, carried for Veterans Day.
geo_headlines: **Pre-open rebound, not a bottom signal:** NQ was 28,350.50 (+1.85%) at 09:29 ET, versus its prior API reference 27,835.25. Its pre-open high reached +2.04%. ES was 7,612.25 (+0.90%) at 09:29 ET. These are pre-open minute bars, not the later tape above.

**An identifiable after-close catalyst:** CoreWeave released results and raised its outlook Tuesday evening, with its conference call at 17:00 ET. That is a concrete AI-demand update; attributing the entire index rebound to one company would overstate the evidence. (CoreWeave investor relations)

**Oil's risk premium remains two-sided:** Reuters' overnight report described oil recovering as continuing Hormuz shipping attacks complicated hopes for de-escalation. The attacks cited were earlier incidents, not newly verified overnight strikes. (Reuters, Nov 11 report)
client_frame_short:
“Does this bounce mean the worst is behind us?” It is encouraging, but **a rebound is not an all-clear**. The technology-heavy futures market recovered before the open, while renewed pressure in oil reminds us that the risks have not disappeared.

We can welcome a better morning without chasing it or abandoning a diversified plan. If your spending needs and risk tolerance have not changed, there is no need to make a portfolio decision because of this bounce alone. We are watching whether the recovery holds through the close, whether participation broadens, and Friday's inflation report.
client_frame:
There is a concrete after-close development to discuss: CoreWeave's results and higher outlook provided a fresh update on AI demand. That supports a more constructive reading of this morning's rebound, but it does not establish that every technology business has the same economics or that selling pressure is exhausted. We have not measured positioning or dealer flows well enough to call this short covering or capitulation. (CoreWeave investor relations)

Keep the time windows straight. Nasdaq futures were up 1.85% just before the cash open; the later snapshot was up 1.56%. Tuesday's semiconductor index close was down 0.35%, and the VIX closed at 19.46. Neither is a reading of today's cash session. A futures rebound and yesterday's volatility close are not enough to declare a durable bottom. (Finance API; Polygon)

The rate backdrop still calls for discipline. The verified policy band is 3.75–4.00%; CME's November 10 cohort assigns December 90% to a quarter-point increase and 10% to a half-point increase. That is a market-implied distribution, not certainty. Treasury cash-market quotes are carried from November 10 because of the Veterans Day closure recommendation, so this edition does not infer fresh bond-market confirmation. (Federal Reserve; CME; SIFMA)

For clients: stay anchored to cash needs, diversification and agreed allocation ranges rather than one morning's direction. Rebalancing toward existing targets is different from chasing a rally. The next checks are closing breadth and leadership, sustained oil pressure, and Friday's 08:30 ET producer-price release; we would reassess if the rebound fails while inflation and financing pressure intensify. (BLS calendar)
